paragraphs: Friend, here's what this whole passage is about: God is near to the ones who are near to Him. Azariah says it plain. "The LORD is with you when you are with Him. If you seek Him, He will be found by you, but if you forsake Him, He will forsake you." (2 Chronicles 15:2) That's not a trick, and it's not a hard-to-find secret. It's an open door, and I would have given anything for an open door back in that junk drawer.

Notice what Asa does with that word. He doesn't nod and go back to his day. He hears it, "took courage," and gets to work, taking out the idols and restoring the altar of the LORD (2 Chronicles 15:8). Then the people make a covenant to seek the LORD "with all their heart and soul," and they rejoice, because they swore it with all their heart (2 Chronicles 15:12, 15). Seeking God isn't a mood, baker. It's a decision you bake into your whole kitchen, with the hard stuff cleared out and the good stuff set back in place.

And hear this part, because it's for you. Even with the high places still standing, Asa's heart was "fully devoted all his days" (2 Chronicles 15:17). A devoted heart doesn't mean a finished to-do list. It means you keep turning toward Him, and Azariah's promise still stands: "be strong; do not be discouraged, for your work will be rewarded." (2 Chronicles 15:7) So seek Him today, friend, and keep seeking tomorrow.
